title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第二十三 王華 王曇首 殷景仁 沈演之
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第二十三 王華 王曇首 殷景仁 沈演之 Volume 63 Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十三 王華王曇首殷景仁沈演之

translations.literal: Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, and Shen Yanzhi

sentences.zh: 王華，字子陵，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Hua, courtesy name Ziling, was a native of Linyi in Langye, a paternal cousin of Grand Tutor Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, whose courtesy name was Ziling, came from Linyi in Langye and was a cousin of Grand Tutor Wang Hong on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 祖薈，衛將軍，會稽內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Guard General and Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had served as Guard General and as interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父，廞，太子中庶子，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: His father Yin was Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had been junior mentor to the heir apparent and left chief clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居在吳，晉隆安初，王恭起兵討王國寶，時廞丁母憂在家，恭檄令起兵，廞即聚眾應之，以女為貞烈將軍，以女人為官屬。

translations.literal: While living in Wu, at the beginning of the Long'an era of Jin, Wang Gong raised troops to attack Wang Guobao. At that time Yin was at home observing mourning for his mother. Gong's proclamation ordered him to raise troops, and Yin immediately gathered followers and responded, making his daughter General of Chaste Valor and appointing women as his staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: The family was living in Wu when, early in the Jin Long'an era, Wang Gong took up arms against Wang Guobao. Yin was then at home in mourning for his mother, but Gong's summons called for troops and Yin at once mustered men to answer it. He made his daughter General of Chaste Valor and staffed his command with women.

sentences.zh: 國寶既死，恭檄廞罷兵。

translations.literal: After Guobao was killed, Gong's proclamation ordered Yin to disband his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guobao was dead, Gong issued a proclamation ordering Yin to stand his forces down.

sentences.zh: 廞起兵之際，多所誅戮，至是不復得已，因舉兵以討恭為名。

translations.literal: When Yin had first raised troops he had put many to death; now he could no longer withdraw and so took up arms under the banner of attacking Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the course of raising his army Yin had executed many people; he could no longer back away, and so he took up arms again, this time in the name of attacking Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭遣劉牢之擊廞，廞敗走，不知所在。

translations.literal: Gong sent Liu Laozhi to attack Yin. Yin was defeated and fled, and his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent Liu Laozhi against him. Yin was beaten and fled, and no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 長子泰為恭所殺。

translations.literal: His eldest son Tai was killed by Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tai was killed on Gong's orders.

sentences.zh: 華時年十三，在軍中，與廞相失，隨沙門釋曇永逃竄。

translations.literal: Hua was then thirteen years old, in the army, and was separated from Yin. He fled with the monk Tan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was only thirteen and with the army when he was separated from his father. He escaped with the monk Tan Yong.

sentences.zh: 時牢之搜檢覓華甚急，曇永使華提衣襆隨後，津邏咸疑焉。

translations.literal: At that time Laozhi was searching for Hua with great urgency. Tan Yong had Hua carry a bundle of clothes and follow behind. Everyone at the ferry crossings was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi was hunting for Hua with great urgency. Tan Yong made the boy carry a bundle of clothes and walk behind him, and at every ferry crossing people grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 華行遲，永呵罵云：「奴子怠懈，行不及我！」

translations.literal: Hua walked slowly, and Yong scolded him, saying, "You lazy slave—you cannot keep up with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Hua lagged behind, and Yong shouted at him, "You worthless slave—you can't even keep pace with me!"

sentences.zh: 以杖捶華數十，眾乃不疑，由此得免。

translations.literal: He beat Hua with a staff dozens of times, and the crowd no longer suspected them, and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Hua with his staff dozens of times until the onlookers no longer suspected them, and in this way Hua was spared.

sentences.zh: 遇赦還吳。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was granted he returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty was declared he returned to Wu.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，以父存亡不測，布衣蔬食不交遊，如此十餘年，為時人所稱美。

translations.literal: In youth he had aspiration and conduct. Because his father's fate was unknown, he wore plain clothes, ate simple food, and made no social visits—for more than ten years—and was praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed purpose and integrity. With his father's fate still unknown, he dressed plainly, ate sparingly, and kept to himself for more than ten years, and people of the day praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲收其才用，乃發廞喪問，使華制服。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu wished to employ his talent and so had Yin's funeral proclaimed and had Hua enter mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu wanted to make use of his abilities, so he announced Yin's death and had Hua put on mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 服闋，高祖北伐長安，領鎮西將軍、北徐州刺史，辟華為州主簿，仍轉鎮西主簿，治中從事史，歷職著稱。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Gaozu on his northern campaign to Chang'an held the post of General Who Guards the West and Governor of Northern Xuzhou; he appointed Hua as Chief Clerk of the province, then transferred him to Chief Clerk of the General Who Guards the West, Attendant Administrative Officer of the Province, and in each office he was outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was over, Gaozu marched north against Chang'an as General Who Guards the West and governor of Northern Xuzhou. He took Hua on as chief clerk of the province, then as chief clerk of his western headquarters, then as attendant administrative officer, and in every post Hua distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮江陵，以為西中郎主簿，遷諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was stationed at Jiangling, he made him Chief Clerk of the General of the West, promoted him to Advising Colonel, and put him in charge of recording affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wen was posted at Jiangling, he made Hua chief clerk of the western headquarters, then promoted him to advising colonel and put him in charge of recording affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖進號鎮西，復隨府轉。

translations.literal: When the Taizu advanced to the title General Who Guards the West, Hua again transferred with the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took the title General Who Guards the West, Hua moved with the headquarters once again.

sentences.zh: 太祖未親政，政事悉委司馬張邵。

translations.literal: Before the Taizu personally administered government affairs, all administration was entrusted to Chief Clerk Zhang Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Before the prince took government into his own hands, he left all affairs to his chief clerk Zhang Shao.

sentences.zh: 華性尚物，不欲人在己前；

translations.literal: Hua by nature prized status symbols and did not wish anyone to rank above him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was vain about appearances and could not bear anyone to outshine him.

sentences.zh: 邵性豪，每行來常引夾轂，華出入乘牽車，從者不過二三以矯之。

translations.literal: Shao was by nature ostentatious; whenever he went out he constantly had paired carriages flank his train. Hua when going out rode in a hand-drawn cart, with no more than two or three attendants, to make a contrast.
translations.idiomatic: Shao loved display and whenever he went abroad had paired carriages escort him. Hua, by contrast, went out in a hand-drawn cart with no more than two or three followers, deliberately playing the opposite part.

sentences.zh: 嘗於城內相逢，華陽不知是邵，謂左右：「此鹵簿甚盛，必是殿下出行。」

translations.literal: Once they met within the city. Hua in the sunlight did not recognize Shao and said to his attendants, "That guard procession is very grand—it must be the Prince going out."
translations.idiomatic: Once they met in the city. Dazzled by the sun, Hua did not recognize Shao and told his attendants, "That procession is enormous—it must be the prince himself going out."

sentences.zh: 乃下牽車，立於道側；

translations.literal: So he left his hand-cart and stood by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down from his cart and stood aside on the road.

sentences.zh: 及邵至，乃驚。

translations.literal: When Shao arrived, he was startled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao drew near, Hua was mortified.

sentences.zh: 邵白服登城，為華所糾，坐被徵；

translations.literal: Shao wearing white mourning dress mounted the city wall and was impeached by Hua; as a result he was summoned and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had gone up on the wall dressed in white mourning, and Hua denounced him for it; Shao was recalled and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 華代為司馬、南郡太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: Hua succeeded him as Chief Clerk, Governor of Nan Commandery, and acting chief of the headquarters and province.
translations.idiomatic: Hua took his place as chief clerk and governor of Nan Commandery, acting head of both headquarters and province.

sentences.zh: 先是，會稽孔甯子為太祖鎮西諮議參軍，以文義見賞，至是為黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had been Advising Colonel of the General Who Guards the West under the Taizu and was admired for literary excellence; by this time he was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had served the prince as advising colonel when he was General Who Guards the West and had won praise for his literary learning. By now he was a gentleman at the Yellow Gate and commandant of foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 甯子先為高祖太尉主簿，陳損益曰：「隆化之道，莫先於官得其才；

translations.literal: Ningzi had earlier been Chief Clerk to Gaozu as Grand Marshal and submitted a statement on what should be cut and what added, saying: "In the way of grand transformation, nothing comes before offices obtaining fit men;
translations.idiomatic: Ningzi had once been chief clerk to Gaozu when he was grand marshal, and he submitted a memorial on what to cut and what to add, saying, "In the path of great transformation, nothing comes before putting the right men in office;

sentences.zh: 枚卜之方，莫若人慎其舉。

translations.literal: In the method of casting lots, nothing surpasses men being strict in their nominations.
translations.idiomatic: and in the method of selection, nothing surpasses men being careful in whom they recommend.

sentences.zh: 雖復因革不同，損益有物，求賢審官，未之或改。

translations.literal: Though the systems of reform differ and cuttings and additions have their objects, seeking the worthy and scrutinizing offices have never been altered.
translations.idiomatic: Systems of reform may differ and what is cut or added may change, but seeking the worthy and scrutinizing officeholders has never gone out of date.

sentences.zh: 師錫僉曰，煥乎欽明之誥，拔茅徵吉，著於幽《賁》之爻。

translations.literal: When the Master consulted and all assented—the radiant charge of reverent clarity; when pulling up grass foretold good fortune—it is set forth in the humble Bi hexagram of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Master took counsel and all assented—how radiant is the charge of reverent clarity; when pulling up grass foretells good fortune—it is written in the humble Bi hexagram of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 晉師有成，瓜衍作賞，楚乘無入，蔿賈不賀。

translations.literal: When Jin's army had success, rewards were made at Guayan; when Chu had no worthy to enter, Wei Jia did not congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's army prevailed, rewards were handed out at Guayan; when Chu had no worthy man to bring in, Wei Jia offered no congratulations.

sentences.zh: 今舊命惟新，幽人引領，《韶》之盡美，已備於振綱；

translations.literal: Now with the old mandate renewed, recluses crane their necks—the perfection of the Shao is already complete in restoring norms;
translations.idiomatic: Now the old mandate is made new and recluses stretch their necks in hope—the perfection of the Shao is already complete in restoring the norms;

sentences.zh: 《武》之未盡，或存於理目。

translations.literal: The imperfection of the Wu perhaps still remains in statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: what the Wu did not finish may still remain in statutes and regulations.

sentences.zh: 雖九官之職，未可備舉，親民之選，尤宜在先。

translations.literal: Though the nine officers cannot all be appointed at once, the choice of those who draw near the people should especially come first.
translations.idiomatic: Though not every post among the nine officers can be filled at once, choosing those who govern close to the people should come first.

sentences.zh: 愚欲使天朝四品官，外及守牧，各舉一人堪為二千石長吏者，以付選官，隨缺敘用，得賢受賞，失舉任罰。

translations.literal: I foolishly wish that every official of the fourth rank at court, and outside them governors and prefects, each nominate one person fit to be chief official at the two-thousand-shi level and deliver him to the selection office to be assigned as vacancies arise; if worthy, the nominator receives reward—if mistaken, the nominator bears punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I would have every fourth-rank official at court, and every governor and prefect in the provinces, each recommend one man fit to serve as a two-thousand-shi chief magistrate, hand the name to the selection office, and let appointments follow vacancies. Reward the nominator when the man proves worthy; punish him when the choice fails.

sentences.zh: 夫惟帝之難，豈庸識所易，然舉爾所知，非求多人，因百官之明，孰與一識之見，執咎在己，豈容徇物之私。

translations.literal: That the Emperor finds it difficult—how could shallow understanding easily achieve it? Yet to nominate those you know is not to seek many men. Relying on the insight of all officials—who can match a single man's knowing? The blame rests on oneself—how can one indulge private favoritism?
translations.idiomatic: Finding the right men is hard even for an emperor—how could shallow minds grasp it easily? Yet to recommend those you know is not to seek a crowd. Which is sharper—the judgment of a hundred offices or the knowledge of one man who must answer for his choice? The blame rests on the recommender; how can he indulge private favor?

sentences.zh: 今非以選曹所銓，果於乖謬，眾職所舉，必也惟良，蓋宜使求賢辟其廣塗，考績取其少殿。

translations.literal: It is not that the Selection Office's adjudication is more regularly in error than nominations by the multitude are invariably good; rather one should have seeking worth open its broad road and evaluation of achievement take the fewest stumbles.
translations.idiomatic: This is not to say that the selection office is always wrong while mass recommendation is always right; rather, open a broad road for seeking talent and let performance review catch the few who stumble.

sentences.zh: 若才實拔群，進宜尚德，治阿之宰，不必計年，免徒之守，豈限資秩。

translations.literal: If talent and substance are outstanding, promotion should emphasize virtue; a magistrate who governs crooked places need not be counted by years; a guard of criminals need not be limited by rank and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: When talent truly stands out, promotion should weigh virtue above all; a magistrate who straightens a crooked district need not be judged by years in office, and a warden of convicts need not be bound by seniority in rank.

sentences.zh: 自此以還，故當才均以資，資均以地。

translations.literal: From this point down, then talent and seniority should be balanced, and seniority and place matched.
translations.idiomatic: Below that level, talent and seniority should be weighed together, and seniority matched to the post.

sentences.zh: 宰蒞之官，誠曰吏職，然監觀民瘼，翼化宣風，則隱厚之求，急於刀筆，能事之功，接於德心，以此論才，行之年歲，豈惟政無秕蠹，民庇手足而已，將使公路日清，私請漸塞。

translations.literal: A magistrate who oversees a district is indeed called an administrative office, yet supervising and viewing the people's afflictions and aiding transformation and disseminating policy—then the demand for hidden depth is more urgent than brush and knife; merit in ability touches upon moral mind; judging talent on this basis, acting by years in office—not only will governance be without waste but the people sheltered like hands and feet; it will also daily clarify the public road and gradually block private requests.
translations.idiomatic: A district magistrate is indeed an administrative post, yet because he watches the people's hardships and helps spread civilizing influence, what is wanted is depth of character more than skill with the brush; real achievement must connect with moral purpose. Judge talent on that basis and let years in office count for something—not only will government be free of rot and the people sheltered like one's own limbs, but the public road will grow clearer day by day and private petitions will gradually be shut out.

sentences.zh: 士多心競，仁必由己，處士砥自求之節，仕子藏交馳之情。

translations.literal: Officials mostly compete in heart—benevolence must come from oneself; retired scholars hone the self-seeking of integrity; officeholders hide the passion of rushing connections.
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen compete in their hearts, benevolence must begin with themselves; recluses will sharpen the integrity of self-reliance, and officeholders will curb the urge to court connections.

sentences.zh: 甯子庸微，不識治體，冒昧陳愚，退懼違謬。」

translations.literal: Ningzi is low and slight, unacquainted with the principles of governance; rashly I present this folly and withdraw in fear of violating truth."
translations.idiomatic: I, Ningzi, am mean and slight and do not understand the principles of government; rashly I offer this foolish counsel and withdraw in fear of error."

sentences.zh: 甯子與華並有富貴之願，自羨之等秉權，日夜構之於太祖。

translations.literal: Ningzi and Hua both had ambitions for wealth and rank. From the time Xu Xianzhi and others held power, day and night they wove plots against them before the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzi and Hua both hungered for wealth and rank. Once Xu Xianzhi and his faction held power, they worked day and night to turn the prince against them.

sentences.zh: 甯子嘗東歸，至金昌亭，左右欲泊船，甯子命去之，曰：「此弑君亭，不可泊也。」

translations.literal: Ningzi once returned east and when reaching Jinchang Pavilion his attendants wished to moor the boat. Ningzi ordered them away, saying, "This is Regicide Pavilion—you cannot moor here."
translations.idiomatic: Once, returning east, Ningzi reached Jinchang Pavilion. His attendants wanted to tie up the boat, but he ordered them on, saying, "This is Regicide Pavilion—we cannot moor here."

sentences.zh: 華每閒居諷詠，常誦王粲《登樓賦》曰：「冀王道之一平，假高衢而騁力。」

translations.literal: Hua whenever at leisure chanted and often recited Wang Can's "Rhapsody on Ascending the Tower": "May I see the King's way leveled to peace, and borrow the high road to exert my strength."
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure Hua would chant poetry and often recite from Wang Can's Rhapsody on Ascending the Tower: "May the royal way be made level and at peace, that I may borrow the high road and stretch my strength."

sentences.zh: 出入逢羨之等，每切齒憤吒，歎曰：「當見太平時不？」

translations.literal: Going out and encountering Xu Xianzhi and others, each time he ground his teeth in rage and sighed, "Will I live to see peaceful times?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad and met Xu Xianzhi and the rest, he would grind his teeth in fury and cry, "Will I ever live to see peaceful times?"

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，甯子病卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Ningzi died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia, Ningzi died of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，誅羨之等，華遷護軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the third year Xu Xianzhi and others were executed. Hua was transferred to Protector of the Army, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xu Xianzhi and his associates were put to death. Hua was made protector of the army while keeping his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 子定侯嗣，官至左衛將軍，卒。

translations.literal: His son Dinghou succeeded to the marquisate, reached office as General of the Left Guards, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dinghou inherited the marquisate, rose to general of the left guards, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子長嗣，太宗泰始二年，坐罵母奪爵，以長弟終紹封。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded; in the second year of Taizong's Taishi era, for cursing his mother he was stripped of the title, and his younger brother Zhong inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded him; in the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, Chang was stripped of his title for reviling his mother, and his younger brother Zhong received the fief in his place.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年，終上表乞以封還長，許之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor, Zhong submitted a memorial asking to return the fief to Chang; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhui under the deposed emperor, Zhong petitioned to return the fief to Chang, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 華從父弟鴻，五兵尚書，會稽太守。

translations.literal: Hua's cousin on the father's side Hong was Minister of the Five Arms and Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's paternal cousin Hong served as minister of the five arms and governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 王曇首，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘少弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Tanshou, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the younger brother of Grand Tutor Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanshou came from Linyi in Langye and was the younger brother of Grand Tutor Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 幼有業尚，除著作郎，不就。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed scholarly attainment; he was appointed Librarian but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed scholarly purpose; he was appointed librarian in the historiography office but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 兄弟分財，曇首唯取圖書而已。

translations.literal: When the brothers divided property, Tanshou took only books and maps.
translations.idiomatic: When the brothers divided the family property, Tanshou took only books and maps.

sentences.zh: 辟琅邪王大司馬屬，從府公脩復洛陽園陵。

translations.literal: He was recruited as Clerk to the Grand Marshal of Langye; he followed the Prince in restoring the imperial tombs at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as an aide to the prince of Langye as grand marshal and accompanied him in restoring the imperial tombs at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 與從弟球俱詣高祖，時謝晦在坐，高祖曰：「此君並膏粱盛德，乃能屈志戎旅。」

translations.literal: Together with his cousin Qiu he visited Gaozu. Xie Hui was then present. Gaozu said, "These gentlemen are both noble scions of eminent virtue—yet they can humble their ambition to military service."
translations.idiomatic: He went with his cousin Qiu to call on Gaozu while Xie Hui was present. Gaozu said, "Both of these men are noble scions of great families, yet they are willing to humble themselves to camp life."

sentences.zh: 曇首答曰：「既從神武之師，自使懦夫有立志。」

translations.literal: Tanshou replied, "Having followed the divine martial master's host, by nature even a coward gains resolution."
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou answered, "Once one has followed a commander of divine martial prowess, even a coward finds his resolve."

sentences.zh: 晦曰：「仁者果有勇。」

translations.literal: Hui said, "The benevolent indeed have courage."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "The benevolent man truly has courage."

sentences.zh: 高祖悅。

translations.literal: Gaozu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 行至彭城，高祖大會戲馬台，豫坐者皆賦詩；

translations.literal: When they reached Pengcheng, Gaozu held a great gathering at Stage for Horse Games; those seated all composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng, Gaozu gave a great banquet at the Stage for Horse Games, and every guest was asked to compose a poem.

sentences.zh: 曇首文先成，高祖覽讀，因問弘曰：「卿弟何如卿？」

translations.literal: Tanshou's text was finished first. Gaozu read it and asked Hong, "How does your younger brother compare with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou finished first. Gaozu read his poem and asked Hong, "How does your younger brother compare with you?"

sentences.zh: 弘答曰：「若但如民，門戶何寄。」

translations.literal: Hong replied, "If he were only like me—on what would the family rely?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong replied, "If he were no better than I, what would become of our house?"

sentences.zh: 高祖大笑。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 曇首有識局智度，喜慍不見於色，閨門之內，雍雍如也。

translations.literal: Tanshou had discernment, capacity, and intelligence; joy and anger did not show on his face; within the women's quarters all was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou had judgment, breadth, and wisdom; pleasure and anger never showed on his face, and within his household all was harmony.

sentences.zh: 手不執金玉，婦女不得為飾玩，自非祿賜所及，一毫不受於人。

translations.literal: His hand did not hold gold or jade; women of the household might not make decorative ornaments; unless from salary and reward, not a hair's worth did he accept from others.
translations.idiomatic: He would not handle gold or jade in his own hands; the women of his house were forbidden ornaments; and except for salary and gifts from the throne, he would not accept the slightest thing from anyone.

sentences.zh: 太祖為冠軍、徐州刺史，留鎮彭城，以曇首為府功曹。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was Champion General and Governor of Xuzhou, stationed at Pengcheng, he made Tanshou Merit Officer of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wen was champion general and governor of Xuzhou, left to hold Pengcheng, he made Tanshou merit officer of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮江陵，自功曹為長史，隨府轉鎮西長史。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was stationed at Jiangling, from Merit Officer he became Chief Clerk, and with the headquarters transferred to Chief Clerk of the General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was posted at Jiangling, Tanshou rose from merit officer to chief clerk, and when the headquarters became General Who Guards the West, he became its chief clerk as well.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚知之，謂太祖曰：「王曇首，沈毅有器度，宰相才也。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew him well and told the Taizu, "Wang Tanshou is deep, resolute, and has capacity—ministerial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thought highly of him and told the prince, "Wang Tanshou is deep, resolute, and broad in capacity—a man fit to be chief minister.

sentences.zh: 汝每事咨之。」

translations.literal: In every matter consult him."
translations.idiomatic: Consult him in everything you do."

sentences.zh: 景平中，有龍見西方，半天騰上，廕五彩雲，京都遠近聚觀，太史奏曰：「西方有天子氣。」

translations.literal: In the Jingping era a dragon appeared in the west, soaring halfway up the sky with five-colored clouds shading it. The capital from near and far gathered to view. The Imperial Historian reported, "In the west there is the aura of a Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingping era a dragon was seen in the west, rising halfway up the sky beneath five-colored clouds. People from all around the capital flocked to look. The imperial astronomer reported, "There is the aura of a Son of Heaven in the west."

sentences.zh: 太祖入奉大統，上及議者皆疑不敢下，曇首與到彥之、從兄華固勸，上猶未許。

translations.literal: The Taizu entered to receive the great succession. The Emperor and all who deliberated were doubtful and dared not descend. Tanshou with Dao Yanzhi and his cousin Hua firmly urged him, but the Emperor still did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince went in to accept the great succession. The emperor and his advisers were all afraid and hesitated to step down. Tanshou, Dao Yanzhi, and his cousin Hua pressed him hard, but the emperor still would not agree.

sentences.zh: 曇首又固陳，並言天人符應，上乃下。

translations.literal: Tanshou again strongly stated it, and also spoke of the correspondence between Heaven and man. Only then did the Emperor descend.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou argued again at length, citing signs of Heaven's approval, and only then did the emperor yield the throne.

sentences.zh: 率府州文武嚴兵自衛，臺所遣百官眾力，不得近部伍，中兵參軍朱容子抱刀在平乘戶外，不解帶者數旬。

translations.literal: He led the military and civil officials of the headquarters and province in strict array to guard themselves. The various officials dispatched from the court—all could not draw near his ranks. Army Adviser Zhu Rongzi embraced his sword outside the Pingcheng gate, not unbuckling his belt for several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: The prince led the civil and military officers of his headquarters and province under strict guard. Officials sent from the court could not approach his ranks. Army adviser Zhu Rongzi stood outside the Pingcheng gate with his sword in his arms and did not unbuckle his belt for several tens of days.

sentences.zh: 既下在道，有黃龍出負上所乘舟，左右皆失色，上謂曇首曰：「此乃夏禹所以受天命，我何堪之。」

translations.literal: Once he had descended and was on the road, a yellow dragon appeared bearing the boat the Emperor rode. His attendants all changed color. The Emperor said to Tanshou, "This is how Yu of Xia received Heaven's mandate—how could I bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication, on the road a yellow dragon appeared and bore up the boat in which the new emperor rode. His attendants turned pale. The emperor said to Tanshou, "This is how Yu of Xia received Heaven's mandate—how am I worthy of such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 及即位，又謂曇首曰：「非宋昌獨見，無以致此。」

translations.literal: When he took the throne he again said to Tanshou, "Had not Song Chang alone seen it, there would have been no reaching this day."
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he said again to Tanshou, "Had you not seen what Song Chang saw, this day would never have come."

sentences.zh: 以曇首為侍中，尋領右衛將軍，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He made Tanshou Palace Attendant and soon let him additionally command the Right Guards and Galloping Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Tanshou palace attendant and soon gave him command of the right guards and of the galloping cavalry as well.

sentences.zh: 以朱容子為右軍將軍。

translations.literal: Zhu Rongzi was made General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rongzi was appointed general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 誅徐羨之等，平謝晦，曇首及華之力也。

translations.literal: The execution of Xu Xianzhi and others and the pacification of Xie Hui were due to the effort of Tanshou and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The execution of Xu Xianzhi and his faction and the pacification of Xie Hui were largely the work of Tanshou and Hua.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，車駕出北堂，嘗使三更竟開廣莫門，南臺云：「應須白虎幡，銀字棨。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia the imperial carriage went out the North Hall and once ordered the Guangmo Gate opened at the third watch. The Southern Office said, "The white tiger banner and silver-character halberd are required."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia the emperor left by the North Hall and once ordered the Guangmo Gate opened at the third watch. The southern office replied, "The white-tiger banner and silver-inscribed halberd are required."

sentences.zh: 不肯開門。

translations.literal: They would not open the gate.
translations.idiomatic: They refused to open the gate.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞羊玄保奏免御史中丞傅隆以下，曇首繼啟曰：「既無墨敕，又闕幡棨，雖稱上旨，不異單刺。

translations.literal: Secretariat Left Assistant Yang Xuanbao memorialized removal of Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and those below. Tanshou followed with a memorial saying, "Since there was no black-ink edict and the banners and halberd were lacking, though it was called the Emperor's intent, it was no different from a lone dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanbao, left assistant of the secretariat, memorialized to dismiss Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and those beneath him. Tanshou followed with a memorial of his own: "Without a written edict in black ink and without the banner and halberd, what was called the emperor's order was no better than a private note.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年、二年，雖有再開門例，此乃前事之違。

translations.literal: In the first and second years of Yuanjia there were precedents of opening the gate twice—yet these were violations of the past.
translations.idiomatic: In the first and second years of Yuanjia the gate was opened twice, but those were departures from precedent.

sentences.zh: 今之守舊，未為非禮。

translations.literal: Today's adherence to the old was not contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To hold to the old rules today was not a breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 但既據舊史，應有疑卻本末，曾無此狀，猶宜反咎其不請白虎幡、銀字棨，致門不時開，由尚書相承之失，亦合糾正。」

translations.literal: But since they relied on former records, there should have been hesitation and submission of the sequence of events—yet never was there such a report; rather one ought to reverse blame on them for not requesting the white tiger banner and silver halberd, causing the gate not to open in time—the fault of the Secretariat's successive handling, which also ought to be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if they were following precedent, they should have paused and reported the full sequence of events—and no such report was made. Rather, blame should fall on those who failed to request the white-tiger banner and silver halberd, so that the gate did not open in time. That was a failure in the secretariat's successive handling, and that too should be corrected."

sentences.zh: 上特無所問，更立科條。

translations.literal: The Emperor especially questioned no one and established new regulations anew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor punished no one in particular and instead drew up new regulations.

sentences.zh: 遷太子詹事，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Steward of the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made steward of the heir apparent while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 晦平後，上欲封曇首等，會宴集，舉酒勸之，因拊御床曰：「此坐非卿兄弟，無復今日。」

translations.literal: After Hui was pacified the Emperor wished to enfeoff Tanshou and others. At a gathering he raised his cup and urged them, and patting the imperial couch said, "This seat—had it not been for you brothers, there would be no today."
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Hui was defeated the emperor wished to enfeoff Tanshou and the others. At a banquet he raised his cup to them and, patting the imperial couch, said, "Had it not been for you brothers, I would not be sitting here today."

sentences.zh: 時封詔已成，出以示曇首，曇首曰：「近日之事，釁難將成，賴陛下英明速斷，故罪人斯戮。

translations.literal: The enfeoffment edict had already been completed and was shown to Tanshou. Tanshou said, "The recent affair—the malice nearly came to fruition; relying on Your Majesty's sagacity and swift decision, therefore the criminals were slain.
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment edicts were already drawn up and shown to Tanshou. He said, "In the recent crisis rebellion was on the verge of success; it was only Your Majesty's swift and wise decision that brought the guilty to execution.

sentences.zh: 臣等雖得仰憑天光，效其毫露，豈可因國之災，以為身幸。

translations.literal: We ministers could rely only on Heaven's light and render our tiny dew—how could we because of the state's disaster make it personal fortune?
translations.idiomatic: We your servants may have lent what little strength we had under your radiance, but how could we turn the state's calamity into private gain?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲私臣，當如直史何？」

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty wished to favor us ministers—what would the upright historiographer do?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty wished to favor us, what would the upright historiographer say?"

sentences.zh: 上不能奪，故封事遂寢。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not override them, and so the enfeoffment matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not prevail, and the enfeoffment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時兄弘錄尚書事，又為揚州刺史，曇首為上所親委，任兼兩宮。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Hong headed the Secretariat and was also Governor of Yangzhou; Tanshou was personally entrusted by the Emperor and his burden straddled both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brother Hong headed the secretariat and was also governor of Yangzhou, while Tanshou was the emperor's personal confidant with duties spanning both palaces.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康與弘並錄，意常怏怏，又欲得揚州，形於辭旨。

translations.literal: Prince Pengcheng Yikang and Hong both headed the Secretariat; he was constantly discontent, and also wanted Yangzhou, which showed in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng Yikang shared secretariat duties with Hong and was constantly displeased; he also wanted Yangzhou, and his resentment showed in what he said.

sentences.zh: 以曇首居中，分其權任，愈不悅。

translations.literal: Because Tanshou stood in the center and divided his power and responsibility, he was still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tanshou stood at the center and shared his authority, Yikang grew still more resentful.

sentences.zh: 曇首固乞吳郡，太祖曰：「豈有欲建大廈而遺其棟樑者哉？

translations.literal: Tanshou firmly begged for Wu Commandery. The Taizu said, "How can one wish to build a great hall yet discard its ridgepole?
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou pressed hard for an appointment in Wu Commandery. The emperor said, "Who would build a great hall and throw away its ridgebeam?

sentences.zh: 賢兄比屢稱疾，固辭州任，將來若相申許者，此處非卿而誰？

translations.literal: Your worthy elder brother has of late repeatedly claimed illness and firmly declined the provincial post; if in future he is allowed to resign, who but you would have this place?
translations.idiomatic: Your worthy brother has lately pleaded illness and refused the provincial post again and again. If I let him step down, who but you should take his place?

sentences.zh: 亦何吳郡之有。」

translations.literal: What need is there for Wu Commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: What need is there for Wu Commandery?"

sentences.zh: 時弘久疾，屢遜位，不許。

translations.literal: At that time Hong had long been ill and repeatedly yielded his post, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hong had been ill for a long time and had repeatedly asked to step down, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 義康謂賓客曰：「王公久疾不起，神州詎合臥治。」

translations.literal: Yikang said to his guests, "Lord Wang has been ill long and does not rise—can the heartland be governed from a sickbed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yikang told his guests, "Lord Wang has been bedridden for ages—can the heartland really be ruled from a sickbed?"

sentences.zh: 曇首勸弘減府兵力之半以配義康，義康乃悅。

translations.literal: Tanshou urged Hong to assign half the headquarters troops to Yikang, and Yikang was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou persuaded Hong to give half the headquarters troops to Yikang, and only then was Yikang satisfied.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 太祖為之慟，中書舍人周赳侍側，曰：「王家欲衰，賢者先殞。」

translations.literal: The Taizu mourned him deeply. Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Zhou Qiu at his side said, "The Wang house will decline—the worthy die first."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply for him. Zhou Qiu, an attendant gentleman of the secretariat, said at his side, "When the Wang house is about to decline, the worthy perish first."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「直是我家衰耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "It is truly my own house that declines."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It is truly my own house that is failing."

sentences.zh: 追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，詹事如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, added Routinely Attached Gentleman, and Steward of the Heir Apparent as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left grand master of splendid happiness and routinely attached gentleman, while retaining his post as steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年，以預誅羨之等謀，追封豫寧縣侯，邑千戶，諡曰文侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for participating in the plot to execute Xu Xianzhi and others, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuning, fief of one thousand households, posthumous title Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, because he had taken part in the plot against Xu Xianzhi and his faction, he was posthumously made marquis of Yuning with a fief of a thousand households and given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，配饗太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was given paired sacrifice in the Taizu temple court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Tanshou was given paired sacrifice in the temple of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 子僧綽嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Sengchuo succeeded; there is a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengchuo succeeded him; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 少子僧虔，昇明末，為尚書令。

translations.literal: His younger son Sengqian, at the end of the Shengming era, was Minister President of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Sengqian, at the end of the Qi Shengming era, served as minister president of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 殷景仁，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Jingren was a native of Changping in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren came from Changping in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖融，晉太常。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong was Jin Grand Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong had been grand director of ceremonies under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，散騎常侍、特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was Attendant Gentleman, Special Advanced, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao had served as attendant gentleman, special advanced, and left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 父道裕，蚤亡。

translations.literal: His father Daoyu died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoyu died young.

sentences.zh: 景仁少有大成之量，司徒王謐見而以女妻之。

translations.literal: Jingren in youth had the capacity for great achievement; Steward Wang Mi saw him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jingren showed the makings of great accomplishment, and Steward Wang Mi, on meeting him, gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 初為劉毅後軍參軍，高祖太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was Rear Army Colonel staff officer under Liu Yi, then Attendant Army Officer under Gaozu as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a staff officer in Liu Yi's rear army, then served as an attendant army officer under Gaozu when he was grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 建議宜令百官舉才，以所薦能否為黜陟。

translations.literal: He proposed that all officials should recommend talent, with promotion and demotion according to whether their recommendations succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that every official should recommend talent and that promotion and demotion should follow whether those recommendations proved sound.

sentences.zh: 遷宋臺秘書郎，世子中軍參軍，轉主簿，又為驃騎將軍道憐主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Secretary of the Song Terrace, Heir Apparent Middle Army Colonel, then Chief Clerk, and again chief clerk to Cavalry General Daoling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretary in the Song secretariat, then middle army colonel to the heir apparent, then chief clerk, and later chief clerk to Cavalry General Daoling.

sentences.zh: 出補衡陽太守，入為宋世子洗馬，仍轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Hengyang, entered as Groom of the Stud to the Song Heir Apparent, and then transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Hengyang, then returned as groom of the stud to the Song heir apparent, and was later made a gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景仁學不為文，敏有思致，口不談義，深達理體；

translations.literal: Jingren's learning was not devoted to literary display; he was keen and thoughtful; he did not discuss principles orally but deeply grasped underlying patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren did not pursue learning for display; he was quick and thoughtful, rarely spoke of doctrine aloud, yet grasped underlying principles with depth.

sentences.zh: 至於國典朝儀，舊章記注，莫不撰錄，識者知其有當世之志也。

translations.literal: As for state statutes, court ritual, old regulations and annotations, he compiled them all—knowing observers saw he had ambition for his age.
translations.idiomatic: On state law, court ritual, and old regulations and commentaries, he compiled and recorded everything, and those who knew him saw that he aimed to serve his own time.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚知之，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew him well and promoted him to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thought highly of him and made him junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太祖所生章太后早亡，上奉太后所生蘇氏甚謹。

translations.literal: The Taizu's birth mother Empress Zhang had died early; the Emperor served Su, whom the Empress Dowager had borne, very carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wen's birth mother, Empress Zhang, had died young, and the emperor served Su, a kinswoman of the empress dowager, with great care.

sentences.zh: 六年，蘇氏卒，車駕親往臨哭，下詔曰：「朕夙罹偏罰，情事兼常，每思有以光隆懿戚，少申罔極之懷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Lady Su died. The imperial carriage went in person to mourn at her bier. An edict said: "I from early suffered partial bereavement; my feelings are doubly ordinary. I constantly think how to glorify honored kin and slightly express boundless grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Lady Su died. The emperor went in person to mourn at her bier and issued an edict: "From early on I have known partial bereavement, and my feelings are all the more ordinary. I have long wished to honor a worthy kinswoman and give some small expression to boundless grief.

sentences.zh: 而禮文遺逸，取正無所，監之前代，用否又殊，故惟疑累年，在心未遂。

translations.literal: Yet ritual texts are lost and scattered; there is nowhere to take standards. Looking to former ages, what was used or rejected again differs—therefore for years I have only doubted, and in my heart the wish has not been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual texts are incomplete and there is no clear standard to follow. Looking to past dynasties, what was adopted or rejected differs again, and so for years I have hesitated without fulfilling what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 蘇夫人奄至傾殂，情禮莫寄，追思遠恨，與事而深，日月有期，將卜窀穸，便欲粗依《春秋》以貴之義，式遵二漢推恩之典。

translations.literal: Lady Su suddenly came to collapse; feeling and ritual have nowhere to rest. Pursuing distant regret, with the affair it grows deep. The days have their term; we shall soon divine the burial mound. I wish roughly to follow the Spring and Autumn principle of honoring by rank and model the Han dynasties' canon of extending favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su has suddenly passed away, and I have nowhere to place my feeling or ritual duty. The more I recall old grief, the deeper it grows with this event. The day of burial draws near, and I wish roughly to follow the Spring and Autumn principle of honoring by rank and to take as model the Han practice of extending favor.

sentences.zh: 但動藉史筆，傳之後昆，稱心而行，或容未允。

translations.literal: But every move relies on the historiographer's brush and is transmitted to later generations; acting as the heart wishes may perhaps not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every act is recorded by the historiographer and handed down to posterity; to act only as the heart wishes may not be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 可時共詳論，以求其中。

translations.literal: Let us at this time discuss it together in detail to seek the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Let us discuss this together now and seek the proper middle course.

sentences.zh: 執筆永懷，益增感塞。」

translations.literal: Taking up the brush I cherish memory forever, and my feeling of blockage only increases."
translations.idiomatic: As I take up the brush my grief only deepens and my heart grows still heavier."

sentences.zh: 景仁議曰：「至德之感，靈啟厥祥，文母俔天，實熙皇祚。

translations.literal: Jingren argued, saying, "The response of utmost virtue moves spirits and opens auspicious signs; the civil mother matches Heaven and truly glorifies the imperial fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren submitted his opinion: "When utmost virtue moves Heaven, spirits reveal auspicious signs; when the civil mother matches Heaven, the imperial fortune is truly made bright.

sentences.zh: 主上聿遵先典，號極徽崇，以貴之義，禮盡於此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reverently follows the former canon, with title at the utmost of emblematic honor; the principle of honoring by rank—ritual is complete in this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reverently follows the ancient canon and has already given the highest honorable title; in the principle of honoring by rank, ritual is already complete.

sentences.zh: 蘇夫人階緣戚屬，情以事深，寒泉之思，實感聖懷，明詔爰發，詢求厥中。

translations.literal: Lady Su by steps of kinship is a relative; feeling because of the affair runs deep—the thought of cold springs truly moves the sage heart. The bright edict is issued and seeks the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su stands only a step removed in kinship, yet feeling runs deep because of the matter; the thought of cold springs truly moves Your Majesty's heart. Your enlightened edict seeks counsel for the proper course.

sentences.zh: 謹尋漢氏推恩加爵，於時承秦之弊，儒術蔑如，自君作故，罔或前典，懼非盛明所宜軌蹈。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the Han practice of extending favor and adding ranks—at that time they inherited Qin's decadence; Confucian learning was scorned; the ruler made precedents himself with none from former canons—I fear this is not what a flourishing clarity should follow.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering the Han practice of extending favor through ennoblement: they had inherited Qin's ruin, Confucian learning was despised, and rulers made precedents as they pleased without ancient models. I fear this is not a path a flourishing age should tread.

sentences.zh: 晉監二代，朝政之所因，君舉必書，哲王之所慎。

translations.literal: Jin looked to the two dynasties as what court governance followed; the ruler's every act is recorded—what wise kings are careful about.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took the two earlier dynasties as its model for court governance; every act of the ruler is recorded—this is what wise kings treat with care.

sentences.zh: 體至公者，懸爵賞於無私；

translations.literal: Those who embody utmost fairness hang ranks and rewards on selflessness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who embody utmost fairness suspend ranks and rewards on impartial merit.

sentences.zh: 奉天統者，每屈情以申制。

translations.literal: Those who uphold Heaven's succession often bend feeling to extend regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who uphold Heaven's mandate often restrain private feeling to uphold the system.

sentences.zh: 所以作孚萬國，貽則後昆。

translations.literal: By this they win trust from all states and leave norms for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they win the trust of all the realm and leave standards for posterity.

sentences.zh: 臣豫蒙博逮，謹露庸短。」

translations.literal: Your servant has received broad inclusion and respectfully offers this shallow view."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has been generously included in this consultation and respectfully offers this humble opinion."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，葬竟，起為領軍將軍，固辭。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended after burial, he was recalled as General of the Palace Garrison and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning and burial, he was recalled as general of the palace garrison but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上使綱紀代拜，遣中書舍人周赳輿載還府。

translations.literal: The Emperor had the administrative officers perform the bow in his stead and sent Attendant Gentleman Zhou Qiu in a carriage to bring him back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his staff perform the ceremony of acceptance on his behalf and sent Zhou Qiu in a carriage to bring Jingren back to his residence.

sentences.zh: 九年，服闋，遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when mourning ended, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when his mourning was complete, he was made vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事劉湛代為領軍，與景仁素善，皆被遇於高祖，俱以宰相許之。

translations.literal: Steward of the Heir Apparent Liu Zhan replaced him as commander of the garrison. He and Jingren had long been on good terms; both were favored by Gaozu and both were regarded as future chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, steward of the heir apparent, replaced him as commander of the garrison. He and Jingren had long been friends; both had won favor under Gaozu and both were expected to become chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 湛尚居外任，會王弘、華、曇首相係亡，景仁引湛還朝，共參政事。

translations.literal: Zhan was still in an outside post when Wang Hong, Hua, and Tanshou died in succession. Jingren brought Zhan back to court to share in government together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was still serving outside the capital when Wang Hong, Hua, and Tanshou died one after another. Jingren brought him back to court so they could share in government.

sentences.zh: 湛既入，以景仁位遇本不逾己，而一旦居前，意甚憤憤。

translations.literal: Once Zhan had entered, because Jingren's rank and treatment had originally not exceeded his own yet suddenly stood before him, his mind was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhan returned, he resented that Jingren—whose standing had never been above his own—had suddenly moved ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 知太祖信仗景仁，不可移奪，乃深結司徒彭城王義康，欲倚宰相之重以傾之。

translations.literal: Knowing the Taizu trusted and relied on Jingren and could not be moved, he then formed deep ties with Steward Prince Pengcheng Yikang, wishing to lean on the weight of a chief minister to overthrow him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor trusted Jingren and would not be swayed, he allied himself closely with Prince Pengcheng Yikang, hoping to use the prince's weight as de facto chief minister to bring Jingren down.

sentences.zh: 十二年，景仁復遷中書令，護軍、僕射如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Jingren was again transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Protector of the Army and Vice Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Jingren was again made director of the secretariat while retaining his posts as protector of the army and vice director.

sentences.zh: 尋復以僕射領吏部，護軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he again held the vice directorship while heading the Ministry of Personnel, Protector of the Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he again headed the ministry of personnel as vice director while keeping his post as protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 湛愈忿怒。

translations.literal: Zhan grew still more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 義康納湛言，毀景仁於太祖；

translations.literal: Yikang accepted Zhan's words and slandered Jingren before the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang took Zhan's side and spoke against Jingren before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖遇之益隆。

translations.literal: The Taizu treated him still more generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated Jingren with still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 景仁對親舊歎曰：「引之令入，入便噬人。」

translations.literal: Jingren said to kin and old friends with a sigh, "I brought him in—and once in, he bites people."
translations.idiomatic: Jingren sighed to relatives and friends, "I brought him in, and the moment he was in he began to bite."

sentences.zh: 乃稱疾解職，表疏累上，不見許，使停家養病。

translations.literal: He then claimed illness and resigned his office, memorial after memorial submitted, but not granted; he was ordered to remain at home and nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and asked to resign, submitting memorial after memorial, but was not permitted to do so and was ordered to remain at home and recover.

sentences.zh: 發詔遣黃門侍郎省疾。

translations.literal: An edict was issued sending a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict sending a gentleman at the Yellow Gate to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 湛議遣人若劫盜者於外殺之，以為太祖雖知，當有以，終不能傷至親之愛。

translations.literal: Zhan proposed sending men like bandits to kill him outside, thinking that though the Taizu knew, he would have his reasons and in the end could not wound the love of closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan proposed sending men disguised as bandits to kill him outside the palace, reasoning that even if the emperor guessed the truth, he would make allowances and could not harm the love between close kin.

sentences.zh: 上微聞之，遷景仁於西掖門外晉鄱陽主第，以為護軍府，密邇宮禁，故其計不行。

translations.literal: The Emperor slightly heard of this and moved Jingren to the residence of the Jin Princess of Poyang outside the Western Gate of the Palace Side, making it his Protector of the Army headquarters, close to the palace inner quarters—therefore their plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor caught wind of this and moved Jingren to the residence of the Jin princess of Poyang outside the western palace gate, using it as his protector's headquarters close to the inner palace, so the plot could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 景仁臥疾者五年，雖不見上，而密表去來，日中以十數；

translations.literal: Jingren lay ill for five years; though he did not see the Emperor, secret memorials went back and forth—by midday there were a dozen or more.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren lay ill for five years. Though he did not appear before the emperor, secret memorials passed to and fro—a dozen or more by midday each day.

sentences.zh: 朝政大小，必以問焉，影跡周密，莫有窺其際者。

translations.literal: Great and small matters of court government were all referred to him; his traces were closely guarded and none could peer into his margins.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter of government, great or small, was referred to him. His movements were kept secret, and no one could see how far his influence reached.

sentences.zh: 收湛之日，景仁使拂拭衣冠，寢疾既久，左右皆不曉其意。

translations.literal: On the day Zhan was arrested, Jingren had his robes and cap brushed clean. He had lain ill so long that those at his side all failed to understand his intent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Zhan was arrested, Jingren had his robes and cap brushed clean. He had been bedridden so long that none of his attendants understood what he meant.

sentences.zh: 其夜，上出華林園延賢堂召景仁，猶稱腳疾，小床輿以就坐，誅討處分，一皆委之。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor went out to Hall for Extending the Worthy in Hualin Garden and summoned Jingren. He still claimed foot ailment and was brought in a small bed-cart to take his seat; execution and disposition of the purge were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor summoned him to the Hall for Extending the Worthy in Hualin Garden. Still claiming a foot ailment, Jingren was carried in on a small couch; the emperor entrusted him with every decision in the purge.

sentences.zh: 代義康為揚州刺史，僕射領吏部如故。

translations.literal: He replaced Yikang as Governor of Yangzhou, Vice Director heading Personnel as before.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Yikang as governor of Yangzhou while retaining his posts as vice director and head of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 遣使者授印綬，主簿代拜，拜畢，便覺其情理乖錯。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to confer seal and ribbon; the chief clerk performed the bow in his stead. When the bow was finished, he at once felt his mind and feelings turn awry.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy brought him the seal and ribbon of office, and his chief clerk performed the bow on his behalf. As soon as the ceremony was over, his mind began to fail.

sentences.zh: 性本寬厚，而忽更苛暴，問左右曰：「今年男婚多？

translations.literal: By nature he had been generous, but suddenly he became harsh and violent. He asked those at his side, "This year are there more male marriages?
translations.idiomatic: By nature he had been mild, but he suddenly turned harsh and violent. He asked his attendants, "This year, are there more sons marrying or more daughters marrying?

sentences.zh: 女嫁多？」

translations.literal: Or more female marriages?"
translations.idiomatic: Or more daughters marrying out?"

sentences.zh: 是冬大雪，景仁乘輿出聽事觀望，忽驚曰：「當閣何得有大樹？」

translations.literal: That winter there was heavy snow. Jingren rode in his carriage out to the office hall to look about and suddenly cried in alarm, "How can there be a great tree in the main gate?"
translations.idiomatic: That winter there was heavy snow. Jingren went out in his carriage to the office hall to look around and suddenly cried, "How can there be a great tree in the gate pavilion?"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「我誤邪？」

translations.literal: Then he said, "Was I mistaken?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "Was I mistaken?"

sentences.zh: 疾轉篤。

translations.literal: His illness turned critical.
translations.idiomatic: His illness grew critical.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂不利在州司，使還住僕射下省，為州凡月餘卒。

translations.literal: The Taizu said it was inauspicious for him to remain in the provincial office and had him return to lodge at the vice director's lower offices; as governor it was little more than a month before he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought the provincial post was unlucky for him and had him return to the vice director's offices at court. He had been governor barely a month when he died.

sentences.zh: 或云見劉湛為祟。

translations.literal: Some said he saw Liu Zhan as a haunting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he was haunted by Liu Zhan's ghost.

sentences.zh: 時年五十一，追贈侍中、司空，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-one. Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, his original offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one. Posthumously he was made palace attendant and minister of works while retaining his former titles.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文成公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Duke of Literary Accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke of Literary Accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 上與荊州刺史衡陽王義季書曰：「殷僕射疾患少日，奄忽不救。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote to Prince Hengyang Yiji, Governor of Jingzhou: "Vice Director Yin was ill only a few days and suddenly could not be saved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote to Prince Hengyang Yiji, governor of Jingzhou: "Vice Director Yin was ill only a few days and then was suddenly beyond help.

sentences.zh: 其識具經遠，奉國竭誠，周遊繾綣，情兼常痛。

translations.literal: His knowledge was comprehensive and far-reaching; serving the state he exhausted loyalty. Our long intimacy makes the feeling doubly painful.
translations.idiomatic: His knowledge was broad and far-sighted, and he served the state with complete loyalty. Our long intimacy makes this loss doubly painful.

sentences.zh: 民望國器，遇之為難，惋歎之深，不能已已。

translations.literal: He was the people's hope and the state's vessel; to meet such a man is rare. My deep regret cannot cease.
translations.idiomatic: He was a pillar of the people's hopes and of the state; men like him are hard to find. My grief is so deep it will not stop.

sentences.zh: 汝亦同不？

translations.literal: Do you feel the same?
translations.idiomatic: Do you feel the same?

sentences.zh: 往矣如何！」

translations.literal: He is gone—what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: He is gone—what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 世祖大明五年，行幸經景仁墓，詔曰：「司空文成公景仁德量淹正，風識明允，徽績忠謨，夙達先照，惠政茂譽，實留民屬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming of Shizu, on an imperial progress passing Jingren's tomb, an edict said: "Minister of Works Duke of Literary Accomplishment Jingren's virtue and measure were deep and upright, his discernment clear and true, his emblematic achievement loyal counsel, early reaching foresight, his benevolent government and abundant reputation truly left in the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu passed Jingren's tomb on tour and issued an edict: "Minister of Works Duke of Literary Accomplishment Jingren was deep in virtue and upright in bearing, clear and trustworthy in judgment, loyal in counsel and far-sighted in service; his benevolent rule and fine reputation truly remain in the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 近瞻丘墳，感往興悼，可遣使致祭。」

translations.literal: Drawing near and viewing the mound and grave, moved by the past I rise in mourning. An envoy may be sent to perform sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Gazing on his mound, I am moved by the past and filled with mourning. Let an envoy be sent to offer sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 子道矜，幼而不慧，官至太中大夫。

translations.literal: His son Daojin from youth was not clever and reached office as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daojin was dull from childhood and rose only to grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 道矜子恆，太宗世為侍中，度支尚書，屬父疾積久，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: Daojin's son Heng, in the Taizong era was Palace Attendant and Minister of Revenue; because his father's illness had long accumulated, he was impeached by the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Daojin's son Heng served as palace attendant and minister of revenue under Emperor Ming; because his father's illness had dragged on, the authorities impeached him.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「道矜生便有病，無更橫疾。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Daojin has been ill from birth; there is no further sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Daojin has been ill since birth; there is no new sudden illness.

sentences.zh: 恆因愚習惰，久妨清序，可降為散騎常侍。」

translations.literal: Heng through stupidity and habitual indolence has long obstructed clear order and may be demoted to Routinely Attached Gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Heng, through folly and habitual laziness, has long neglected his duties and may be demoted to routinely attached gentleman."

sentences.zh: 沈演之，字台真，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yanzhi, courtesy name Taizhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi, whose courtesy name was Taizhen, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 高祖充，晉車騎將軍，吳國內史。

translations.literal: Ancestor Chong was Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry and Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Chong had been general of chariots and cavalry under Jin and interior minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勁，冠軍陳祐長史，戍金墉城，為鮮卑慕容恪所陷，不屈節，見殺，追贈東陽太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jin was chief clerk to Champion Chen You, garrisoning the city of Jinyong; he was taken by the Xianbei Murong Ke, would not submit, and was killed; posthumously given Governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jin was chief clerk to Champion Chen You and held Jinyong when the Xianbei general Murong Ke took the city. He refused to yield and was killed, and was later posthumously made governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 祖赤黔，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chiqian was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chiqian had been minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 父叔任，少有幹質，初為揚州主簿，高祖太尉參軍，吳、山陰令，治皆有聲。

translations.literal: His father Shuren in youth had capacity and substance; at first he was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou, Army Officer under Gaozu as Grand Marshal, and magistrate of Wu and Shanyin—his governance in each had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuren showed ability from youth. He first served as chief clerk of Yangzhou, then as an army officer under Gaozu when he was grand marshal, and as magistrate of Wu and Shanyin, winning praise in every post.

sentences.zh: 朱齡石伐蜀，為齡石建威府司馬，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu, he was Chief Clerk of Lingshi's headquarters as General Who Establishes Might, with additional title General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu, Shuren served as chief clerk of his headquarters as general who establishes might and was given the additional title of that same rank.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之功，亞于元帥，即本號為西夷校尉、巴西梓潼郡太守，戍涪城。

translations.literal: In the merit of pacifying Shu he was second only to the commander-in-chief; on his original title he was Colonel of the Western Yi, Governor of Brazil and Zitong commanderies, garrisoning Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Shu his merit was second only to the commander-in-chief. He was made colonel of the western Yi and governor of Brazil and Zitong, and garrisoned Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 東軍既反，二郡強宗侯勱、羅奧聚眾作亂，四面雲合，遂至萬餘人，攻城急。

translations.literal: Once the eastern army had rebelled, powerful clans of the two commanderies Hou Mo and Luo Ao gathered followers and made disorder; from all sides they clouded together until they reached more than ten thousand men and pressed the siege urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern army rebelled, the powerful clan leaders Hou Mo and Luo Ao of the two commanderies raised troops in revolt. Men converged from every side until they numbered more than ten thousand and pressed the siege hard.

sentences.zh: 叔任東兵不滿五百，推布腹心，眾莫不為用，出擊大破之，逆黨皆平。

translations.literal: Shuren's eastern troops were fewer than five hundred; he extended trust with open heart and none did not serve him. Going out he struck and greatly defeated them; the rebel faction was all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shuren had fewer than five hundred men in the east, but he won every man's loyalty with open-hearted trust. He went out, routed them completely, and pacified the rebels.

sentences.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，齡石遣叔任率軍來會。

translations.literal: When Gaozu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Lingshi sent Shuren to lead troops and join the rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Lingshi sent Shuren with troops to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 時高祖領鎮西將軍，命為司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu held the post of General Who Guards the West and appointed him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then general who guards the west and appointed Shuren his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，以為揚州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was made Attendant Administrative Officer, Vice Director of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made attendant administrative officer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀全涪之功，封寧新縣男，食邑四百四十戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying Shu and preserving Fucheng intact, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningxin, fief of four hundred forty households.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Shu and holding Fucheng intact, he was enfeoffed as baron of Ningxin with a fief of four hundred forty households.

sentences.zh: 出為建威將軍、益州刺史，以疾還都。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Yizhou; because of illness he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as general who establishes might and governor of Yizhou, but returned to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Yixi, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 長子融之，蚤卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rongzhi died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rongzhi died young.

sentences.zh: 演之年十一，尚書僕射劉柳見而知之，曰：「此童終為令器。」

translations.literal: When Yanzhi was eleven, Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Liu saw him and recognized him, saying, "This boy will in the end be fine material."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi was eleven, Liu Liu, vice director of the secretariat, met him and said at once, "This boy will become a great man."

sentences.zh: 家世為將，而演之折節好學，讀《老子》日百遍，以義理業尚知名。

translations.literal: His family for generations were generals, but Yanzhi restrained himself and loved learning, reading the Laozi a hundred times a day, and was known for esteeming principles and reason.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been military for generations, but Yanzhi curbed his pride and devoted himself to learning. He read the Laozi a hundred times a day and became known for his devotion to principle and reason.

sentences.zh: 襲父別爵吉陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's separate enfeoffment as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Jiyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's separate title as fifth-rank marquis of Jiyang county.

sentences.zh: 郡命主簿，州辟從事史，西曹主簿，舉秀才，嘉興令，有能名。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk to the commandery prince, recruited as Attendant Administrative Officer of the province, Western Bureau Chief Clerk, recommended as Outstanding Talent, magistrate of Jiaxing—with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the commandery prince, was recruited as an attendant administrative officer of the province, became chief clerk of the western bureau, was recommended as outstanding talent, and was magistrate of Jiaxing, winning a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 入為司徒祭酒，南譙王義宣左軍主簿，錢唐令，復有政績。

translations.literal: He entered as Libationer of the Secretariat, Left Army Chief Clerk to Prince Nanqian Yixuan, magistrate of Qiantang—again with achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as libationer of the secretariat, then served Prince Nanqian Yixuan as chief clerk of the left army and as magistrate of Qiantang, again with a strong record in office.

sentences.zh: 復為司徒主簿。

translations.literal: Again he was Secretariat Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He again became chief clerk of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起為武康令，固辭不免，到縣百許日，稱疾去官。

translations.literal: Recalled as magistrate of Wukang, he firmly declined but could not avoid it; after reaching the county about a hundred days, he claimed illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as magistrate of Wukang, declined firmly but could not refuse, and after barely a hundred days in the county claimed illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除司徒左西掾，州治中從事史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Left Western Clerk of the Secretariat and Attendant Administrative Officer of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was over he was made left western clerk of the secretariat and attendant administrative officer of the province.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，東諸郡大水，民人饑饉，吳義興及吳郡之錢唐，升米三百。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies suffered great flood; the people were in famine—in Wu, Yixing and Qiantang in Wu commandery, rice was three hundred cash per sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies were flooded and the people starved. In Yixing and Qiantang in Wu, rice reached three hundred cash per sheng.

sentences.zh: 以演之及尚書祠部郎江邃並兼散騎常侍，巡行拯恤，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and Jiang Sui, Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, were both additionally made Routinely Attached Gentlemen to tour and relieve, permitted to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and Jiang Sui of the ministry of rites were both given the additional post of routinely attached gentleman to tour the region and bring relief, with authority to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 演之乃開倉廩以賑饑民，民有生子者，口賜米一斗，刑獄有疑枉，悉制遣之，百姓蒙賴。

translations.literal: Yanzhi then opened granaries to relieve the starving; for those who bore sons, each person was given one dou of rice; doubtful and wrongful cases in punishment and prison were all released—the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi opened the granaries to feed the hungry. Families with new births received a dou of rice for each mouth, and doubtful or wrongful prisoners were all released. The people owed him their survival.

sentences.zh: 轉別駕從事史，領本郡中正，深為義康所待，故在府州前後十餘年。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Administrative Officer, heading the provincial impartial judge; deeply treated by Yikang, so at headquarters and province for more than ten years before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He became attendant administrative officer and head of the provincial impartial judge. Deeply favored by Yikang, he remained at headquarters and in the province for more than ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 後劉湛、劉斌等結黨，欲排廢尚書僕射殷景仁，演之雅仗正義，與湛等不同，湛因此讒之於義康。

translations.literal: Later Liu Zhan, Liu Bin and others formed a faction wishing to expel and ruin Vice Director Yin Jingren; Yanzhi by nature relied on righteousness and differed from Zhan and others—Zhan therefore slandered him to Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Zhan, Liu Bin, and others formed a faction to drive out Vice Director Yin Jingren. Yanzhi stood on principle and broke with them, and Zhan therefore slandered him to Yikang.

sentences.zh: 嘗因論事不合旨，義康變色曰：「自今而後，我不復相信！」

translations.literal: Once in discussion of affairs they did not accord with the intent; Yikang changed color and said, "From now on I no longer trust you!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when their discussion of policy failed to please him, Yikang turned dark and said, "From now on I will no longer trust you!"

sentences.zh: 演之與景仁素善，盡心於朝庭，太祖甚嘉之，以為尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and Jingren had long been on good terms and devoted their hearts to the court; the Taizu greatly praised this and made him Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi had long been close to Jingren and gave his full loyalty to the court. The emperor praised him highly and made him gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十七年，義康出籓，誅湛等，以演之為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Yikang went out to his fief, Zhan and others were executed, and Yanzhi was made General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yikang left for his fief, Zhan and his faction were executed, and Yanzhi was made general of the right guards.

sentences.zh: 景仁尋卒，乃以後軍長史范曄為左衛將軍，與演之對掌禁旅，同參機密。

translations.literal: Jingren soon died; then Rear Army Chief Clerk Fan Ye was made General of the Left Guards to pair with Yanzhi in commanding the forbidden guard and share in secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren soon died, and Fan Ye, chief clerk of the rear army, was made general of the left guards to share command of the palace guard with Yanzhi and to join him in confidential counsel.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷侍中，右衛將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Palace Attendant, General of the Right Guards as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made palace attendant while retaining his post as general of the right guards.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂之曰：「侍中領衛，望實優顯，此蓋宰相便坐，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: The Taizu said to him, "Palace Attendant commanding the guard—reputation and substance are superior and prominent; this is virtually the chief minister's seat of honor. Strive in it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "As palace attendant commanding the guard, your standing is eminent and bright. This is virtually the chief minister's seat. Do your utmost in it."

sentences.zh: 上欲伐林邑，朝臣不同，唯廣州刺史陸徽與演之贊成上意。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to attack Linyi; court ministers differed—only Governor of Guangzhou Lu Hui and Yanzhi supported the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to attack Linyi. Most court ministers disagreed, but Governor Lu Hui of Guangzhou and Yanzhi alone supported the plan.

sentences.zh: 及平，賜群臣黃金、生口、銅器等物，演之所得偏多。
