translations.literal: When it was pacified, gold, captives, bronze vessels and such were given to the ministers—Yanzhi's share was comparatively more.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign succeeded, the emperor gave gold, captives, bronze vessels, and the like to his ministers, and Yanzhi received a larger share than most.

sentences.zh: 上謂之曰：「廟堂之謀，卿參其力，平此遠夷，未足多建茅土。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him, "In court planning you shared in the effort; pacifying these distant barbarians is not enough to build many fiefs of earth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "You shared in the court's planning, but pacifying these distant peoples is not enough to merit many new fiefs.

sentences.zh: 廓清京都，鳴鸞東岱，不憂河山不開也。」

translations.literal: Clearing the capital region and sounding the imperial bells at Mount Tai—you need not worry that rivers and mountains will not open."
translations.idiomatic: When the capital is cleared and the imperial procession sounds at Mount Tai, you need not fear that the realm will not open before us."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔曰：「總司戎政，翼贊東朝，惟允之舉，匪賢莫授。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict said, "Overall command of military affairs, aiding and assisting the eastern palace—such trusted appointment is given to none but the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year an edict declared, "To command military affairs and aid the eastern palace is a trust given only to the worthy.

sentences.zh: 侍中領右衛將軍演之，清業貞審，器思沈濟。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant commanding the Right Guards Yanzhi—pure conduct and faithful scrutiny, capacity and thought deep and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and general of the right guards Yanzhi is pure in conduct, firm in judgment, and deep and steady in mind.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍曄，才應通敏，理懷清要。

translations.literal: General of the Right Guards Ye—talent responding with penetrating keenness, reason embracing clarity and essentials.
translations.idiomatic: General of the right guards Ye is quick and penetrating in talent and clear and exact in judgment.

sentences.zh: 並美彰出內，誠亮在公，能克懋厥猷，樹績所蒞。

translations.literal: Both beauty manifests within and sincerity shines in public service—able to exert their merit and establish achievement where they preside.
translations.idiomatic: Both show excellence within and integrity in public service, and are able to fulfill their duties and build achievement in every post they hold.

sentences.zh: 演之可中領軍，曄可太子詹事。」

translations.literal: Yanzhi may be Central Commander of the Army; Ye may be Steward of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi is fit to be central commander of the army; Ye is fit to be steward of the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 曄懷逆謀，演之覺其有異，言之太祖，曄尋事發伏誅。

translations.literal: Ye harbored a treacherous plot; Yanzhi sensed his strangeness and spoke to the Taizu; Ye soon's affair broke out and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye harbored treasonous designs. Yanzhi sensed something amiss and reported it to the emperor. Ye's plot was soon exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 遷領國子祭酒，本州大中正，轉吏部尚書，領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Libationer of the National University, Great Impartial Judge of the province, then Minister of Personnel, additionally commanding Right Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became libationer of the national university and great impartial judge of his province, then minister of personnel and commander of the heir apparent's right guard.

sentences.zh: 雖未為宰相，任寄不異也。

translations.literal: Though not chief minister, his trust and commission were no different.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was not formally chief minister, the trust placed in him was no less.

sentences.zh: 素有心氣，疾病歷年，上使臥疾治事。

translations.literal: He had long had heart qi ailment; illness lasted years—the Emperor had him conduct affairs while ill in bed.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from heart trouble and was ill for years, yet the emperor had him conduct affairs from his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 性好舉才，申濟屈滯，而謙約自持，上賜女伎，不受。

translations.literal: By nature he loved raising talent and extending help to the blocked and stalled, yet maintained modest restraint; the Emperor gifted female performers and he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to advance talent and help those who had been passed over, yet he remained modest and restrained. When the emperor gave him female performers, he refused them.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，車駕拜京陵，演之以疾不從。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the imperial carriage worshipped at the capital tombs; Yanzhi from illness did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor went to worship at the capital tombs, but Yanzhi did not accompany him because of illness.

sentences.zh: 上還宮，召見，自勉到坐，出至尚書下省，暴卒，時年五十三。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned to the palace and summoned him to audience; exerting himself he reached his seat; going out to the lower offices of the Secretariat he suddenly died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace he summoned Yanzhi, who forced himself to attend. After leaving the audience he reached the lower offices of the secretariat and died suddenly, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 太祖痛惜之，追贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰貞侯。

translations.literal: The Taizu grieved and prized him; posthumously he was given Routinely Attached Gentleman and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply for him and posthumously made him routinely attached gentleman and grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 演之昔與同使江邃字玄遠，濟陽考城人。

translations.literal: Yanzhi once with fellow envoy Jiang Sui, courtesy name Xuanyuan, a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi had once served as envoy together with Jiang Sui, courtesy name Xuanyuan, from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 頗有文義。

translations.literal: He had considerable literary understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He had considerable literary learning.

sentences.zh: 官至司徒記室參軍，撰《文釋》，傳於世。

translations.literal: He reached office as Recording Colonel of the Secretariat and composed Literary Explication, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to recording colonel of the secretariat and wrote Literary Explication, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 演之子睦，至黃門郎，通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's son Mu reached Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Direct and Routinely Attached Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's son Mu rose to gentleman at the Yellow Gate and direct, routinely attached gentleman.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明初，坐要引上左右俞欣之訪評殿省內事，又與弟西陽王文學勃忿鬩不睦，坐徙始興郡，勃免官禁錮。

translations.literal: Early in Daming of Shizu, for summoning and drawing in the Emperor's attendant Yu Xin to inquire and comment on inner-palace affairs, and for quarreling with his younger brother Prince Xiyang's literary attendant Bo, he was exiled to Shixing commandery; Bo was dismissed from office and forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, Mu was exiled to Shixing for drawing the emperor's attendant Yu Xin into discussions of inner-palace affairs and for feuding with his younger brother Bo, literary attendant to the prince of Xiyang. Bo was dismissed and placed under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 勃弟統，大明中為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Tong, in the Daming era was Assistant Gentleman of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger brother Tong served as assistant gentleman of writings under Daming.

sentences.zh: 先是，五省官所給幹僮，不得雜役，太祖世，坐以免官者，前後百人。

translations.literal: Earlier, the dry servants given to officials of the five directorates could not do miscellaneous labor; in the Taizu era those dismissed from office for this numbered a hundred before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the dry servants assigned to officials of the five directorates were forbidden to perform miscellaneous labor. Under Emperor Wen, about a hundred officials were dismissed for violating this rule.

sentences.zh: 統輕役過差，有司奏免。

translations.literal: Tong's light service exceeded the norm; the responsible offices memorialized dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Tong overworked his servants beyond what was allowed, and the authorities memorialized for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔曰：「自頃幹僮，多不祗給，主可量聽行杖。」

translations.literal: Shizu edicted: "Lately dry servants mostly do not respect their supply—masters may as a measure permit carrying staff."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu decreed, "Lately dry servants have often failed in their duties. Masters may, within reason, apply the staff to them."

sentences.zh: 得行幹杖，自此始也。

translations.literal: Permission to apply staff to dry servants—from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: Permission to beat dry servants began from that time.

sentences.zh: 演之兄融之子暢之，襲寧新縣男。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's elder brother Rongzhi's son Changzhi inherited the barony of Ningxin county.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi, son of Yanzhi's elder brother Rongzhi, inherited the barony of Ningxin.

sentences.zh: 大明中，為海陵王休茂北中郎諮議參軍，為休茂所殺，追贈黃門郎。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he was Advising Colonel to Prince of Hailing Xiumao as Northern Army and was killed by Xiumao; posthumously given Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daming he served Prince Hailing Xiumao as advising colonel of the northern army and was killed by the prince. He was posthumously made gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 子曄嗣，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Ye succeeded; when Qi received the mandate, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye succeeded him; when Qi took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：元嘉初，誅滅宰相，蓋王華、孔甯子之力也。

translations.literal: The historian says: At the beginning of Yuanjia the execution and destruction of chief ministers was largely the doing of Wang Hua and Kong Ningzi.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: At the beginning of Yuanjia the destruction of the chief ministers was largely the work of Wang Hua and Kong Ningzi.

sentences.zh: 彼群公義雖往結，恩實今疏，而任即曩權，意非昔主，居上六之窮爻，當來寵之要轍，顛覆所基，非待他釁，況於廢殺之重，其隙易乘乎！

translations.literal: Those dukes in justice had past bonds but in grace were now distant; their office was yesterday's power, their mind not yesterday's lord—standing in the exhausted hexagram above six, at the critical track of coming favor, the foundation of overturning needed no other opening; how much more when the weight is execution and ruin—the gap is easy to ride!
translations.idiomatic: Those lords still had old ties of justice, but imperial favor had grown thin. They held yesterday's power without yesterday's standing with the throne. They stood in the exhausted position of the upper sixth line, on the very verge of losing favor. The ground for overturning them needed no other pretext—and how much more when the issue was execution! The opening was easy to seize.

sentences.zh: 夫殺人而取其璧，不知在己興累；

translations.literal: To kill a man and take his jade disc, not knowing the trouble raised in oneself;
translations.idiomatic: To kill a man and take his jade disc, unaware of the trouble one raises for oneself;

sentences.zh: 傾物而移其寵，不忌自我難持。

translations.literal: to overturn things and shift favor, not fearing difficulty in holding oneself.
translations.idiomatic: to overturn the established order and shift imperial favor, heedless of how hard it will be to hold one's own position.

sentences.zh: 若二子永年，亦未知來禍所止也。

translations.literal: If the two sons had lived out their years, one still would not know where coming calamity would stop.
translations.idiomatic: Had those two men lived out their years, who can say where later disaster would have ended?

sentences.zh: 有能戒彼而悟此，則所望於來哲。

translations.literal: If one can warn of that and awaken to this, that is what is hoped from coming sages.
translations.idiomatic: If later men can take warning from their example and understand this lesson, that is what the historian hopes for.
